title: Smoke harness hangs on a failed server boot: stop() awaits an exit that already fired, so the suite ends on an unsettled top-level await (exit 13) with no summary line
note: Proven root cause of the release step reporting no result. tools/smoke-test.mjs stop() did `child.on('exit', resolve)` on an already-dead child and relied on an .unref()'d 8s timer that can never fire once the loop is idle -> promise never settles -> node exits 13, skipping both the summary line and process.exit(1). Separately waitForHealth polled its full 120x500ms budget (measured 56.2s) and threw a message that named no cause. Fixed: stop() skips the wait when child.exitCode/signalCode is already set and clears a ref'd escalation timer on exit; waitForHealth takes an optional supervised server and fails immediately with the server's own stderr tail. Also drained startExtraServer's piped-but-never-read stderr (lost diagnostic plus a full-pipe stall risk). New tools/harness-selftest.mjs (npm run test:harness) drives the real smoke-test.mjs against the real server.js with its port held, so it works installed or bare. Measured 56222ms/exit 13/4 fail -> 555ms/exit 1/4 pass, and confirmed by reinstating the bug.

title: The other 11 waitForHealth call sites can still burn the full 60s budget on a dead server
note: New idea, found while fixing the above. superviseServer()/waitForHealth(url, supervised) now exist and are wired at the two shared helpers (start, startExtraServer), but 11 per-group spawn sites in tools/smoke-test.mjs (lines ~257, 498, 753, 1137, 1263, 1490, 1706, 1762, 1984, 2024, 2160) still call waitForHealth(url) with no process handle, so a group whose server dies costs a minute and names no cause. Each already holds `proc` on the preceding lines, so each is a one-token change: waitForHealth(url, superviseServer(proc)). Most also hand-roll the same log-capture array that superviseServer replaces, so this also removes duplication. Deliberately left out of this round to keep the diff to one production file backed by the measured reproduction.

title: A negative Playwright step duration is passed straight through to the API, and the smoke suite fails on it after a cold browser launch
note: New idea, observed once this round with evidence. On the first-ever chromium launch after `npx playwright install chromium`, `SMOKE_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1 npm test` failed `a run records per-step durations and the step that failed` with `Launch browser` reporting durationMs: -885 (also Before Hooks -662, Fixture "browser" -883). Attribution was checked three ways: pristine HEAD harness warm = 150/0/0, this round's harness warm = 150/0/0, this round's harness cold = 149/1. So it tracks the cold launch, not the diff -- but the underlying cause (WSL2 clock step during the post-install first launch is the suspicion) was NOT proven and it reproduced only once. The durable defect regardless of trigger: server.js:1196 (the generated reporter) and server.js:1252 (flattenReportSteps) both do `typeof step.duration === "number" ? step.duration : null|undefined`, so a negative value Playwright emits is published verbatim; tools/smoke-test.mjs:2850 asserts the contract is `null || >= 0`. server.js:2421 (`last?.duration ?? null`) reads the same value for the test level and must be handled in the same change -- per the rule about two paths reading one value, do not fix only one. Not attempted this round because there is no deterministic reproduction to drive a failing test from, and normalizing without one risks masking rather than fixing.

title: Recording dedupe swallows distinct selectOption/press steps
note: Carried over, still valid, not touched this round. server.js startRecording (~7355) onEvent compares only previous.value === step.value, but selectOption carries step.values and press carries step.key, so a second selection on the same select within 600ms is silently dropped and the recording replays the wrong option. Widen the comparison signature to [action, locator, value, values, key]. Needs a browser: recording checks all SKIP without one. Chromium is now installed in this worktree, which removes the download cost that made this risky right after a TIMEOUT round.

title: npm test in a bare checkout does not tell you to run npm install
note: Partly addressed as a side effect this round and should be re-scoped rather than done as written. The harness now reports `server process exited (code 1, signal null)` followed by the server's own stderr tail, which includes `Cannot find module 'swagger-ui-dist/package.json'` -- so the cause is stated and it arrives in 0.5s instead of 56s. What is still missing is the actionable sentence: detect a missing node_modules up front and say `run npm install`. Much smaller now that the diagnostic plumbing exists.

title: check() double-reports group-level and check-level SKIP as two lines
note: Carried over, still valid, not touched. tools/smoke-test.mjs ~1324/1557/1845 call record('<group> checks','skip',...) and then also return 'skip', so check() prints a second line and the skipped tally counts one event twice. Note the scout's premise was wrong: there is no { skip: reason } return path on HEAD (a2a44d4) -- check() only recognises the bare string 'skip', so that path has to be added first. Changing this moves the skipped count, which other records' expected values depend on, so it wants its own round.

title: recorderLocatorCandidates double-escapes quotes into an invalid CSS selector
note: Carried over, not re-verified this round. server.js:3832 replaceAll('"', '\\"') yields [name="a\\"b"]. Only elements whose name/id contains a quote are affected, so the input is rare. Per the operator rule on two parsers reading the same value, the page_inspect path that builds the same selector has to be checked end-to-end in the same change, which is what makes this bigger than it looks.

title: Recording nth note overwrites the ambiguous note
note: Carried over, still unverified. server.js startRecording sets step.note on ambiguous and the following resolved.nth branch overwrites it. Whether the two conditions can co-occur is still unconfirmed; confirm first and drop to rejected if they cannot, rather than changing code speculatively.
